title: Songbook and Letters
author: U. M. Iversen
blurb: Quentin Montrose, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter and part-time novelist, swears the heart is a muscle like any other: trainable, containable. Then two estranged names appear on the same impossibly stubborn orchard deed — and he is pulled straight into the middle of it. To get through this, he must say the sentence that has been rehearsed for a decade before the festival ends.
style: atmospheric and lyrical, with strong sensory detail
